items.title: Vampire Survivors' Best Replacement Officially Launches in 2 Weeks
items.summary: The new game, due out on Nov. 10, is described as "Warhammer meets Vampire Survivors."
items.content:
By Ashley Potter Published Oct 28, 2026, 4:30 AM EDT Ashley blends more than three decades worth of love of video games with more than 10 years of professional journalism experience. She has written and edited for multiple outlets, including HardcoreGamer and MassLive , and loves blending her passion for video games with her drive to tell human interest stories. Polygon writer Justin McElroy , in his 2022 review of the game, described it as "a deliciously perfect pairing that seems all but self-evident once you’ve tried it."

Now Poncle, the independent studio behind Vampire Survivors , is back, alongside Auroch Digital, with a game described as " Warhammer meets Vampire Survivors ." Promising the same "bullet heaven" gameplay popularized by Vampire Survivors, Warhammer Survivors is officially due out on Nov. 10 — around the same time as both the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Grand Theft Auto 6 .

The game will feature more than 40 playable characters from across the Warhammer 40K and Age of Sigmar universes, each with their own unique weapons and stats.

Of course, a game described as "bullet heaven" is nothing without its arsenal, and players will have over 75 weapons to choose from, ranging from the Boltgun to Astartes chainswords. In a love letter to Warhammer hobbyists, players can even fight off hordes of enemies with Nuln Oil, which flings black liquid down onto the battlefield, damaging groups of enemies and making them more vulnerable to fire damage. (It's inspired by the black paint hobbyists use to shade Warhammer miniatures.)

Taking a page from the highly-praised accessibility of its predecessor, Warhammer Survivors offers a low barrier to entry. The game costs only $7.99 to preorder on Steam , where a free-to-play demo is also available for download. The game will also be available to play on Android, iOS, Nintendo Switch & Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. Actual store prices may vary by platform and region, and select stores may have preorder or launch-day discounts.

items.content:
If you've ever wondered what a fusion of Vampire Survivors and Heroes of Might and Magic would look like, then Heroes Never Die might be the game for you. It's a newly announced fantasy strategy game from developer Ludogram that "aims to take the best of the survival formula and fuse it with more tactical decisions, real-time army building, and powerful fantasy heroes." It will be released in 2027 for PC.

In Heroes Never Die, you'll choose your titular hero – there are over 20 in the lineup – and battle not just monster hordes but also rival heroes. Each hero has their own skills, but no matter who you pick, you'll seek to upgrade your town by gathering resources and fighting foes. There are also four factions and over 60 different units, with the developers promising that no two runs will be alike.

“We’re delighted to finally announce Heroes Never Die, a project we’ve been working on in the shadows for a couple of years”, said creative director Edouard Gaudel. “We cannot wait to see our first players fighting hordes of monsters, and evolving their armies while meeting our heroes. Don’t forget to join our upcoming Playtest!”

If you're interested, you can sign up for the private playtest and/or wishlist Heroes Never Die on Steam .

items.title: Everything you need to know about Warhammer Survivors: release date, trailers, platforms, and much more
items.summary: We recently learned that the spinoff is heading to a bunch more platforms.
items.content:
With a brand-new demo now available for Steam Bullet Fest, it seems the wait for Warhammer Survivors may not be much longer.

This highly anticipated crossover between Auroch Digital (Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun, Boltgun 2 and Words of Vengeance), poncle (Vampire Survivors), and Warhammer has understandably generated plenty of excitement, and we couldn’t be more hyped.

With release drawing closer, we’ve put together a handy guide. Below you can find answers to the most pressing questions relating to its confirmed champions, enemy factions, the release date, and more.

Warhammer Survivors offers a faithful take on the survivor-style formula, developed in collaboration with poncle, the studio behind Vampire Survivors.

Players face endless waves of enemies as a cast of renowned champions taken from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer: Age of Sigmar universes.

The game is said to feature an arsenal of familiar weapons, such as the Boltgun, Astartes Chainsword, Whirlwind Axes. It will also include multiple modes and stages from across the grim, dark 41st Millennium and the Mortal Realms.

You might be wondering why this wasn’t released as a Vampire Survivors DLC. According to the developers in a Steam blog, the project contains far too much content to be delivered as an expansion. In the blog, the team said:

“It’s built on the foundation of Vampire Survivors, but every single character, stage, enemy, powerup and secret has been built from scratch to create an experience that exists alongside the traditional Vampire Survivors experience.”

The entire roster for Warhammer Survivors is yet to be revealed, but we do know some champions that will appear from both universes.

More characters are expected to be revealed as we approach launch.

As well as the many champions, we do know some of the enemy factions that we will be battling our way through.

The Skaven are a race of subterranean Ratmen who dwell in rotten warrens, conducting twisted experiments combining machinery, magic, and mutation. Now unleashed upon the Mortal Realms, they swarm forth with corrupted machines and mutants in search of Warpstone.

The Tyranids are a Xenos bioform species that have invaded the galaxy from beyond the void. Clad in thick chitin and armed with lashing tendrils, razor-sharp talons, and terrifying symbiotic weaponry, they represent a relentless and horrifying threat.

Seen stomping through the new Ork Stronghold stage, the Orks are a brutal mob of boisterous bullies who overwhelm players with waves of varied enemy types. From Grots and Bomb Squigs to Ork Boyz and Lootas, they unleash relentless “dakka” across the battlefield.

items.title: What on Earth Is Happening to 'Diablo II'?
items.summary: ©Blizzard EntertainmentBlizzard Entertainment's 'Diablo II' remains a classic game beloved by many gamers to this day.In 2021, it gained new life with the release of 'Diablo II: Resurrected', which improved graphics and quality of life.
items.content:
From Survivor-likes to VR, a Genre-Bending Transformation

Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ©Blizzard Entertainment Blizzard Entertainment's 'Diablo II' remains a classic game beloved by many gamers to this day.

In 2021, it gained new life with the release of 'Diablo II: Resurrected', which improved graphics and quality of life. Recently, however, a rather strange transformation has been occurring around the game. Moving beyond simply adding new items or classes, a series of attempts are emerging that alter the game's perspective, controls, and even its core genre.

The most striking example is the recently revealed 'D2 Survivors'. As the name suggests, it is a fan game that reimagines Diablo II as a survivor-like in the style of 'Vampire Survivors'. While utilizing the graphics, sound, and characters of the original game, its gameplay is vastly different. Players move to dodge swarms of demons while slaying enemies with automatically triggered skills, powering up their characters by choosing new abilities each time they level up.

It doesn't merely borrow Diablo II's outer appearance, either. The seven classes, various skills, and item systems from the original game are all implemented, along with regions spanning five acts as well as Nightmare and Hell difficulties. D2 Survivors is an unofficial, free fan project that loads graphics and sounds directly from the Diablo II or Diablo II: Resurrected game files owned by the player. Thanks to this approach, anyone who owns the original game can play it not only through a standalone program but directly inside a web browser as well.

Meanwhile, another case has emerged that fundamentally changes how players view Diablo II. Released in September by developer emmericp, 'D2R-3D' is a mod that allows players to freely rotate and zoom the fixed quarter-view camera of Diablo II: Resurrected. Breaking away from the traditional isometric perspective looking down at the character, players can observe combat from behind or up close, taking in Sanctuary as a fully perspective-rendered 3D space. However, early standalone versions faced issues such as shutting down after about one minute due to game integrity checks, making it more of an experimental endeavor than a polished feature.

What is interesting is that this perspective modification led to yet another experiment. Evolving from ideas sparked by D2R-3D, the 'D2R VR' project enables Diablo II to be played using virtual reality headsets. Going beyond simply projecting the game screen into a VR space, it implements features such as swinging weapons or drawing bows in first-person view and aiming spells with hand motions. In effect, it turns a quarter-view hack-and-slash RPG into an immersive action RPG.

Attempts to make the graphics even more realistic have also been added to the mix. A recently shared video demonstrates Diablo II: Resurrected—modified to a 3D camera—with Nvidia's DLSS 5 neural rendering technology applied externally. It is an experiment to alter screen lighting and material textures without completely recreating the original game's terrain and characters. However, this is also closer to a tech demonstration achieved by modders combining existing technologies rather than an officially supported feature.

What makes these developments even more fascinating is that these distinct attempts have surfaced one after another in a relatively short period. On one side, Diablo II was converted into a survivor-like; on another, the camera was liberated, which in turn paved the way for VR controls. Unlike traditional modding that adds content or tweaks balance in the original game, experiments that reshape the very way players experience the game are now unfolding around a single title.

Of course, attempts to change the genre of classic games are not entirely new. 'Lambda Wars', which brought the 'Half-Life 2' universe into a real-time strategy game, was released in 2014, while 'Age of Doom', which recreated Doom using the 'Age of Empires II' engine, appeared in 2021. The culture of using a game's engine and assets to create an entirely different work has existed for a long time. However, the recent momentum surrounding Diablo II catches attention because individual experiments are connecting with one another to generate new possibilities.

That is not to say these projects have reached a level where they can immediately replace the original game. Forcibly modifying the game's structure can lead to stability or compatibility issues, and using original game assets requires careful consideration of copyright and terms of service. Moreover, changing the perspective alone does not automatically reshape the game's combat design to match, so being technically feasible is a separate matter from providing a polished gameplay experience.

Even so, the fact that a game over 25 years old is transforming in such diverse ways is quite remarkable. A game where players once endlessly clicked their mice to hunt demons is now becoming a survivor-like where they dodge horde after horde, or a game where they put on VR headsets to swing swords themselves. Blizzard's Diablo II may have been completed long ago, but it seems gamers are far from finished coming up with new ways to play with it.

items.title: Vampire Crawlers Is the Perfect Example of a “Spooky, Not Scary” Game
items.summary: Vampire Crawlers is a great example of "spooky, not scary," or something with the atmosphere and vibes of horror but no actual scares.
items.content:
Scrolling through Netflix some years ago, I noticed a category that perfectly describes a specific type of movie or television show I often enjoy watching: “spooky, not scary.” At the time, the category featured shows like Stranger Things and films such as Shaun of the Dead . Without even reading a description of the category, I understood immediately from what was included that it featured shows and movies that had the atmosphere, imagery, and overall vibes of horror, but weren’t actually meant to scare viewers.

It occurred to me, then, that so much of what I loved watching growing up fit distinctly into this genre, especially since I rarely enjoy (or even watch) actual horror films. For example, my favorite Disney animated film might be The Nightmare Before Christmas , since it has all the classic monsters and darkness you might find in classic horror, yet never actually scared me as a child. I mostly enjoyed the music and the creepiness, as I also did with cartoons like Aaahh!! Real Monsters and Courage the Cowardly Dog .

The same is largely true when it comes to my love of video games. Despite adoring a handful of unambiguously terrifying games (e.g., Dead Space , Inside , several Resident Evil titles), so many of my favorite games to play during October wouldn’t scare a child but still have the essence of horror within them. Notable examples obviously include the Castlevania franchise, Luigi’s Mansion , Metroid Fusion , the Hearts of Stone expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , Inscryption , classic DOOM , and Carrion .

It makes perfect sense, then, that this month I have fully embraced what I believe is 2026’s best “spooky, not scary” game: Vampire Crawlers .

Waves and Waves and Waves Poncle’s Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors is a roguelike deck-builder that expands upon Poncle’s excellent 2022 autobattler Vampire Survivors (which, itself, took most of its inspiration from Castlevania ) to create a consistently and intensely spooky experience. To be clear, though: It’s not scary at all, and that’s part of the fun.

Much like in Vampire Crawlers , the player selects a “crawler” with whom to start a run and utilizes the various strengths of each possible crawler to make their way through treacherous locales (such as haunted forests and creepy mansions). From a first-person perspective, the player navigates these labyrinthine environments while fighting waves of vampire bats, animated skeletons, gargoyles, and other typical monsters in turn-based combat using cards they pick up along the way.

It’s almost like I’m playing through a gamified Halloween party. Sure, there’s references to blood, death, and fright, but it’s all set dressing; I’m just here to have a good time.

The actual battles are fairly straightforward yet have the potential for remarkable depth. You only have a handful of cards at a time and limited mana to use per turn on such cards, and the cards you start your run with are fairly basic and easy to understand (e.g., “gain 2 armor” or “deal 30 damage to a likely attacker”). Combat scenarios range from a small group of vampire bats to seemingly endless waves of evil golems followed by an intensely difficult boss.

As one might expect from a roguelike, Vampire Crawlers ratchets up the complexity the more you progress through each stage, with the ability to alter various cards’ abilities, add to your mana total, and collect newer, more powerful cards. If you play your cards right (get it?) and formulate the right strategy around cards and crawlers, you could end up dealing over 1,000 damage each turn, giving yourself enough armor to basically make you impervious to enemy attacks, or even turning one turn into three in a row with no enemy retaliation in between.

Plenty of Haunts, but No Frights The actual gameplay loop of Vampire Crawlers is mostly simple, but the little bits of complexity build up into an endlessly thrilling and engaging experience, one that firmly has its hooks in me. Every time I start a new run, it feels like the world around me stops moving as I walk through spooky, dimly-lit hallways in haunted mansions, castles, and even dairy-processing facilities. I’m laser-focused on the next wave of enemies and searching for little secrets in every corner. I barely notice that, to some extent, these enemies and objects around me are meant to scare and intimidate me.

Therein lies the brilliance of Vampire Crawlers’ setting: It’s got spooky skeletons, bloodthirsty bats, and menacing minotaurs at every turn, yet everything feels fun and inviting. Part of it is the videogaminess of everything — after all, I’m still healing my crawler with a roasted chicken I found on the floor — but another part is the loop itself. The abilities the cards afford you and the ease of early encounters create a sense of power over everything that approaches you, so the pixelated monsters never come off as all that horrifying at all. It’s almost like I’m playing through a gamified Halloween party. Sure, there’s references to blood, death, and fright, but it’s all set dressing; I’m just here to have a good time.

Closing Thoughts Ultimately, I think that’s why the “spooky, not scary” atmosphere works so well for me. Games in the genre feel like a costume party, or even a Halloween-themed stage play where I’m one of the actors. The purpose of the spooky environment is less to scare me and more to give the addictive gameplay loop a little more flamboyance and flair. This comes in contrast to more traditional horror games like Dead Space , where I’m fighting against my own fear of death and solitude as much as I’m fighting giant space monsters.

I don’t know if I’ll ever truly love horror as a genre. Each new Resident Evil I play or movie like Obsession I watch brings me a little closer to fully embracing these types of stories, but I doubt I’ll ever get to the point where I consume whatever frightening tales come my way. Until then, I’ll spend my Octobers with kitschy, non-terrifying games like Vampire Crawlers , which give me the thrills and vibes of horror without any feelings of fear or panic.

Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors , developed by Poncle and Nosebleed Interactive and published by Poncle, released on April 21, 2026, for PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 1 & 2, and iOS.

items.summary: Even as we drown in Warhammer games, Survivors stands out as something extremely cool.

Having spent 10 hours with its demo, however, I'm increasingly convinced that it deserves to be catagorised as a sequel.

A lot of care has clearly gone into the hero design, maps and all the horrible beasties trying to eviscerate you, and rather than simply replicate Vampire Survivors, Auroch Digital has included a bunch of novelties and new ideas, like followers and more overt boss battles.

Playing it on my Steam Deck has already had a terrible impact on my sleep routine, just like its predecessor. And with its launch just around the corner on November 10, I think I'm just going to have to accept that I'm going to be very tired for the rest of the year.

Weapon evolutions, enemies that drop chests with multiple items, arcana, bosses, challenges, upgrades—if it's in Vampire Survivors, it's probably in Warhammer Survivors, albeit with some Warhammer-themed twists. Instead of experience gems, for instance, you get experience skulls (because of course you do). And instead of Red Death, you get Extremis bosses, massive seemingly invincible bastards—until you figure out the trick to destroying them.

I have used buckets of Nuln oil in my Warhammer painting endeavours—and yes, I've spilled a lot of it. On my jeans, on my carpet, one time on my dog. But it's never hurt anyone. In Warhammer Survivors, it's been weaponised, damaging and slowing ememies, as well as making them more flammable. You'll also be able to get your hands on explosive dice, which roll across the battlefield before going kaboom! I'm sure there are rules against this.

The first WH40k map sees you running around a battlefield that's being swallowed up by tyranids. It's aggressively pink and full of horrible pustules and grotesque alien topography. In Age of Sigmar, meanwhile, it's skaven time! Nasty little rodents, glowing warpstones, you know the deal. There's even a map that's just your tabletop, full of paints and measuring tape, where all the game's monstrosities gather together to take you out.

While Warhammer Survivors is a singleplayer romp, that doesn't mean you're all alone. Unlockable characters can be rescued once you defeat the enemies harassing them, after which they'll join you in battle. In subsequent fights, they'll rejoin you when you select one of their associated weapons when you level up. At least one character gets buffs from having more followers, and upgrading his lasgun also lets him run around with his fellow Astra Militarum grunts.

I've poured hundreds of hours into Vampire Survivors, and Warhammer Survivors might be a bit trickier. Battles escalate a lot faster, and it took me longer to figure out good weapon combos that worked to thin the herd. I was a lot more desperate for healing than I'm used to with its predecessor. I think I'd prefer the early game to be slightly less intense, though the issue might be that the demo features fewer weapons and characters, which could be making it feel a touch more challenging than it actually is.

Enemy factions benefit from unique traits that may give you a bit of a hard time. Tyranids, for instance, can be empowered by more intelligent members of their species, which use their synapse power to enrage lesser critters within their radius. So you'll want to take these psychic beasties down quickly. Orks, meanwhile, can get all riled up, kicking off a WAAAGH, where they spawn in greater numbers and become faster and stronger.

When you play Warhammer Survivors, you select a universe first. Characters, upgrades and unlocks are specific to each universe, though you will find some passive abilities repeated in both. It feels like two spin-offs collected in a single game.

Vampire Survivors is the game that really justified my purchase of a Steam Deck, and while developer Auroch Digital still says it's working on compatibility, it already feels great on my Deck. It's where I've spent most of my time playing it and I've got no complaints.

Cancel all of your plans in November, because Warhammer Survivors is launching on the 10th. And I've got high hopes for it. Yes, it's a spin-off, but it also feels like a proper Vampire Survivors sequel and potentially my favourite bullet heaven since the OG.

items.title: Acclaimed Vampire Survivors-Inspired Survival Game Hits Switch Next Month
items.content:
If you're one of many people who got hopelessly addicted to Vampire Survivors , then you might want to keep an eye out for Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor , which launches on Switch on 9th October 2026 .

Developed by Funday Games, DRG: Survivor launched in early access on 14th February 2024 before receiving a full release on Windows and Xbox Series X|S on 17th September 2025. It's been well-received too, earning a score of 8/10 from IGN and 90% from PC Gamer , with the latter concluding its review with a line that will undoubtedly catch your attention:

"Vampire Survivors is no longer the king of the genre."

So yeah, sounds pretty good. But what's it all about? Well, as a spin-off of the 4-player co-op shooter Deep Rock Galactic , DRG: Survivor uses auto-shooting mechanics to fend off hordes of enemies, uncover valuable loot within the mines, and upgrade your characters with powerful new abilities.

It's chaotic, it's colourful, and it's very pretty, so we're really looking forward to checking this out on Switch.

items.title: How Vampire Survivors became Vampire Crawlers: Six lessons from building a game based on another developer's IP
items.summary: Nosebleed Interactive's Andreas Firnigl on crafting a spin-off of Poncle's smash hit: pub prototypes, shared rules, last-minute changes and more
items.content:
Nosebleed Interactive's Andreas Firnigl on crafting a spin-off of Poncle's smash hit: pub prototypes, shared rules, last-minute changes and more

Image credit: Nosebleed Interactive/Poncle Academy by Andreas Firnigl CEO, Nosebleed Interactive Published on Aug. 10, 2026, 3:19 p.m. Follow Nosebleed Interactive Andreas Firnigl started his career as a tester on Big Mutha Truckers, way back on Gamecube. He founded Nosebleed Interactive almost 15 years ago as CEO and creative director.

In 2023, an old contact I had worked with 15 years ago – and who is now at Poncle – came to us with the amazing opportunity to collaborate on a Vampire Survivors spin-off.

Luca Galante, the creator of Vampire Survivors, had come up with the idea for a card game spin-off and had already developed an early prototype, but Poncle wanted an external studio to help turn it into a complete game. So lead designer Luke Wintflint and I worked with Luca and Poncle to evolve that idea into what became Vampire Crawlers.

After 15 years making games and working with other studios, Nosebleed Interactive has learnt a lot about how to treat someone else's IP and how to collaborate with external partners. We learnt even more on Crawlers, and I want to share some key lessons that you can take away and apply at your own studio.

Naturally, understanding the IP you are working on is vital. Yet it's even more important to demonstrate to the client that you understand it.

I've put a stupid amount of hours into Vampire Survivors in order to understand all the little nuances and tics that most people won't notice. This kind of intense playing helps you to understand what is changeable and what is not. Some things will be fundamental to the experience and will have to be incorporated, while others are things that, frankly, players don't care about all that much. Knowing what can and can't be changed is a sign you are working on something you understand, rather than doing a half-arsed superficial imitation.

The fundamentals of Vampire Crawlers came together very quickly. A pen and paper version that we played in the pub during the early days of development was surprisingly close to the final game. However, in those early months, we paid less attention to the IP and were instead focused on adding content, throwing in random stuff willy-nilly as a placeholder. We knew it would be quick and easy to fix later on, and knew enough about the IP to do it right – but Poncle didn't.

We had the bones of a great game, but it wasn't clear to Poncle that we had a good Vampire Survivors game. So we downed tools on everything else and focused on fixing that – making sure all the names were right, matching up how stats would transfer from Survivors to Crawlers, and so on. As soon as Poncle saw the next build, they gave us the green light.

In short, do that work of understanding your partner's IP – but make sure you show them you have that understanding, too.

Fans of the IP will naturally be interested in playing your new game, but you also need to make sure it works for people who don't know the original title. This is why it's important to get feedback from people who haven't played the IP at all.

There were a couple of people at Nosebleed who hadn't played Vampire Survivors, and rather than encouraging them to try the game, we asked them to avoid playing it at all. Having some folks on the team who are coming in clean, as it were, was a real help to balance the onboarding, which is so important in this kind of game. Relying too much on knowledge of the existing IP could make it less attractive to new players.

Your partner is working with you because you have something to bring to the table (there's certainly a lot of Nosebleed's DNA in Vampire Crawlers). So lean into your strengths – but be humble. Be prepared to learn from how your partner works, and what works for their IP.

Before Crawlers, we'd just come off Arcade Paradise, where the density of every pixel had to be exactly correct. Would Poncle do that? No.

items.title: Here are five Vampire Survivors-likes so that you can live forever
items.summary: Vampire survivors has a lot of imitators. Here are five excellent choices for those who can't get enough of the genre.
items.content:
I’ve played a lot of Vampire Survivors , including the vast majority of its DLC and I’m looking forward to the Warhammer spin-off due later this year too. Finding myself hooked on the survive-’em-up subgenre — and yes I will refer to them as that instead of “bullet heaven”, don’t try and stop me — means that I’ve played a lot of similar games. Some are weaker offerings like Cyberheroes Arena DX , but there are a rampaging horde of above average choices. So here I’ve compiled five excellent choices that offer something a little different to the genre leader, but are also tremendous fun in their own right.

Starting with what is probably the closest game to Vampire Survivors on this list, Army of Ruin features all the bright colours, fun looking enemies, and simple move and autoshoot gameplay. It’s a solid system that works well and the visuals are surprisingly impressive for what is arguably a simple game. The main gameplay twist here is that you also have an active ability that can attack enemies around you before needing to reset with a cooldown timer. Each character has their own one, as well as a personal weapon and unique stats.

And boy are there a lot of characters, weapons, and items! You unlock new things at a hell of a clip, with individual levels offering you specific challenges that will give you gold for stat buffs or new weapons and characters. I liked knowing where I needed to focus my efforts to get a new fun toy to play with. Additionally, levels have difficulty options as well, with you getting to scale up how hard it is to access new challenges for unlocks. There’s a ton of content here, and I’ve barely scratched the surface in spite of dozens of hours playing.

Something that also uses the active ability system and builds on it further is R.I.P . You unlock active abilities by levelling up as you’d expect, deploying them when you need to, ideally when facing one of the many bosses. These feel powerful and can really turn the tide if used correctly. There’s a hell of a tide to turn here too, with hordes of zombies bearing down on you right from the off. Interestingly, enemies here have to actually attack you rather than relying on contact damage, meaning you can prepare yourself a little more readily, assuming you can get your timing right with the sheer volume incoming.

The extra twist here, aside from the lovely grimdark aesthetic, is that you also have to aim your attacks. Most survive-’em-ups are content to just let you fire freely and not worry, but not in R.I.P. You’ll need to pick your targets to get the most out of your weapons, and those that are directly beneath your crosshair will suffer additional damage. This forces you to actually consider accuracy and not just dodgeroll around everywhere. It’s challenging, but the visuals certainly get my attention.

Another grimdark style game, but this time with a fantasy setting is Halls of Torment . My initial feelings on this one weren’t great, but the Diablo -esque art style appealed and I gave it a chance. This one does a great job of actually making your enemies feel threatening, as they aren’t just numerous, but also powerful. Your choice of hero heavily dictates how you’ll handle them too, with a ranged fighter and a melee fighter playing in genuinely different ways rather than in Vampire Survivors where certain weapon choices can negate specific playstyles.

There’s a much bigger focus on story here too, with excursions into the titular halls often being to rescue a character to add to your town or about finding an item to unlock new levels of the halls. You have to plan for your mission too, as you’ll want to be aiming for these objectives, and some characters will be better equipped to handle them. I liked the inclusion of actual — albeit it simple — puzzles to acquire some of your objectives. There’s a lot to like here, and the art style really does a good job of bringing it all together.

From grimdark to literally everything in the universe! Everything is Crab isn’t necessarily about crabs unless you evolve into a crablike creature. This one is wildly different to other genre offerings, with you evolving your creature constantly throughout a twenty-or-so minute run. On the surface, that wouldn’t be a lot different, but the sheer variety of different evolutions is mindboggling. The illustrious Reuben Howe describes it best with “… having 12 charmed creatures, many of whom were ferrets, while my main mouthpiece was a leech maw and my legs were tentacles turned me into an eldritch horror. ” which is a hell of a way to end a run.

Unlike others in the genre, considering how many evolutionary paths there are, Everything is Crab requires much more planning, and isn’t simply a game in which you get stronger because attacks hit harder. You’ll need to pick out complimentary evolutions to give yourself a fighting chance as your run continues. The bright, playful art style certainly helps to keep things interesting. I can understand why pixel art was the choice as there’s no way anyone has the time to create and animate that number of different creatures!

My favourite one to finish. It helps that I really like Deep Rock Galactic as a base game, but even that lends itself very nicely to the survive-’em-up genre. You’re a dwarf, doing what dwarves do and mining all the goodies you can out of a planet. Sadly, the planet doesn’t like that and just so happens to be swarming with bugs of different varieties who are happy to kill you. You’ll level up, tool up, and shoot up the monsters as you try to mine all the resources you can to pursue meta progression for new characters and weapons.

The twist here is that you can mine any rocky surface you can find. Yes, mining gold to aid your run is useful, but if you’re backed into a corner, you can dig your way backwards while blasting bugs at the same time. Very satisfying when you manage to get out of a tight spot. Each stage ends with a rush to your drop pod to head ever deeper, before finally taking on a boss or blowing up a huge chunk of planet to take home. The weapons feel great, and you’re constantly unlocking more and better options as you might expect. The only downside I have here is that the enemy variety is occasionally a bit lacking.

I’m sure there are plenty of other excellent ones that I simply haven’t got to (yet). I’m told Megabonk is a lot of fun and Yet Another Zombie Survivors looks pretty good too, so with any luck I’ll find time to survive even more!

items.content:
Hi everyone, we have a lot happening around new games and Vampire Survivors, so here's a gigantic news post! 🟣- Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton 🔴- Vampire Survivors 1.15 🔴- Legacy of the Bloodmoon teasers 🔴- Legacy of the Moonspell info 🔴- Workshop Support for Vampire Survivors 🔴- ARG and Character Community Challenge winners 🔴- Vampire Survivors Comics 🔵- Vampire Crawlers updates 🟢- PoncleUp

🟣 Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton

A few days back we announced Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton in collaboration with Shueisha Games! Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game like Vampire Survivors, but with a twist: you'll be able to play an 8-player survivors royale PvPvE mode! Some in-game names and terminology are still in development and may be subject to change. While every player plays in their own world, you accumulate points by defeating curses and sorcerers, and with every 100 points accumulated you get to choose a Rule Change that can affect everyone's game. Some Rule Changes are INSANE, but for now we'll just reveal the simple ones you can see in the trailer (silence, slow, steal points...). But Rule Changes aren't the only way to interact with other players. Introducing a world first, mind blowing, unbelievable game mechanic: PRESS A BUTTON. While you move your auto-attacking character, your special attack also builds up. By PRESSING A BUTTON when the special attack is ready, you get to unleash your character's Special Attack, or, if that character can, a DOMAIN EXPANSION! Other players can be caught in the effect of your Domain or Special Attack, so you have to keep an eye on other players' position and special-bar status. A very important aspect of the 8-players mode is the Live Match Status Feed (working name). This big chunk of UI on the left side of the screen constantly updates in real time, acting not only as a scoreboard, but also sending out warnings and all kind of information about what the other players are up to. At the end of the 15 minutes battle royale, the 2 players with the most points will face one another in a 19 seconds duel. Despite the online focus, Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game you can also play alone, in a mission-based mode, just like Vampire Survivors. If you don't ever want to go online, you'll still be able to play the 8-players battle royale mode against bots. This is a game you buy once and can play anytime. We'll keep supporting the game after launch, with our usual style of content updates. So forget about gatcha elements or a forever-evolving PvP meta keeping your time and wallet hostages: our focus here are fun and affordability. Apologies if you had enough of this wall of text, but I kepty mouth shut for almost two years and I haven't even got to the technical bits yet! Yes, the game runs on the Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton framework, so you can expect that same familiar experience playing it, but we had to do several unique tweaks for Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble Survivaton. Other than the obvious, completely new networking for the gameplay and Live Match Status Feed, we have doubled the resolution at which the game runs. That allowed us to completely rebuild the whole VFX pipeline so that we could re-create the distinctive look of Curse Energy and the changes the whole stage depending on activated Domain Expansions or Special Attacks. Another reason to double the resolution was to properly display the UI (that has been completely reworked at framework level) and the Live Match Status Feed, that is capable of also streaming gameplay snippets from other online players. You'll see a lot of other tweaks, like the fact that characters look different if they are seen from the left or from the right, a "default attack" per character that triggers without any weapon, or walls that are actually solid to name a few. Then there are other changes that won't be noticeable until you get to play the game. For example, while we are going by the same content-unlock-philosophy as Vampire Survivors, we are completely reworking the progression in the various game modes and also per-character, so that every game mode will feel fresh even to VS veterans. That's all for now, I hope you have enjoyed the trailer; my favourite part was that bit were Gojo takes a walk.

- Nintendo Switch 1 and 2 - Android - iOS & Apple Arcade - PS4 and PS5 - Xbox - EGS In the following weeks there will be small updates quite often on all platforms to bring them all on the same version, because all platforms have the same content, but not the same bugfixes and tweaks. Please join the Discord or keep an eye on the Updates version of the wiki if you're interested in knowing the fixes in each update (I won't spam Steam News every week for small tweaks).

When we'll launch Legacy of the Bloodmoon, we'll also update the contents of Legacy of the Moonspell. It will get 7 new unlocks, that will deliver:

  • 4 new weapons: LunarMight, LunarSight, LunarBight, and LunarFlight [/*]

🔴 Bloodmoon character tease

Legacy of the Bloodmoon is almost complete and we will be able to start testing and submissions soon! That means we'll have an actual release date soon too. In the meantime, here's a Character Spotlight video about Malice Bloodmoon:

🔴 ARG and Community Character Competition winners

Congratulations to the trio of winners of the Lucca Comics ARG: Jenoss, Miryel, Siming, and GIU_LLS (:poemg:?), and to DissonantSynth for winning the Community Challenge! We're finally getting into the design stage of the characters, with a first implementation that will soon be shared with the winners, behind the scenes, to start iterating together on gameplay mechanics. You can expect a few surprises and little extras about them when they'll make their appearance in the game! Baron Husker and Sefi Rotto (:poemg:?) will come alive in a later update, v1.17

Instead of waiting the conclusion of the current cycles of updates for Vampire Survivors as originally planned, we will develop modding support over time, one feature at a time. Feature 1 will be about adding CUSTOM (private/local) and WORKSHOP (public/Steam Workshop) characters! Please join the Discord or use the public-beta forum if you're interested in trying out custom characters before they go live on the main branch, in a future update (currently aiming for v1.17)

Vampire Survivor is getting comics! We've been working with Titan Comics on a 4-issue series, written by David Hazan and illustrated by Jimm Kucaj, with the first issue coming out this September, available in 3 cover variants. Some familiar Vampire Survivors will go through Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, and a few other places, and there might even be some lore in there. Issue #1 is available to pre-order from your local comic shop or from Forbidden Planet if you're in the UK / EU. You can find out more about the comics on the Titan Comics website.

🔵 Vampire Crawlers: first QOL update

Our first update to Vampire Crawlers add an Endless mode and several QOL improvements! You can find more details, the strategy behind future updates, and some content spoilers in the Steam News here.

🟢 Countup to the next announcement

Look, we're doing a lot of stuff across several small teams. I'm always happy to write the Steam News but I cannot bombard your feed with everything we're doing. Also took me something like 3 weeks to set this all up. So if you'd like to hear about what we're doing a bit more often, then please visit poncleup.com to see a recap or subscribe to our newsletter. It's a countup instead of a countdown because, as you might have noticed, we're release-date-averse and have no idea ourselves when we'll drop something new 🤷‍♂️ Just know that the newsletters are written by the marketing team :vsskull: Alright, I'm done with work, time to go back having fun on my secret project. Thank you everyone, I'll leave you in the self-proclaimed capable hands of the marketing team! - Luca

items.content:
Hi everyone! As anticipated several months ago, we’ve been working on several core systems of VS to be able to keep making more content, increase stability, and improve performance. It’s been a while so we have quite a few things to cover today: - a new expansion for VS - a new update - a new poncle team in Japan - the very sensible reason why Vampire Survivors has a sub-title now 🤷‍♂️

Vampire Survivors Update 1.15 (The Wet One) is out now on Steam!

You can find all details about 1.15 below, now here’s a stupid summer trailer about it:

Major QOL improvements

  • Multiple Save Slots (about time!)
  • Character Setup panel for skins, egg selection, etc…
  • Content filters in Character Selection and Unlocks menu
  • Stability improvements for late game and low-end platforms
  • Reduced loading times (more noticeable on other platforms than PC)

New content

  • 1 New Stage: The Lycaeum
  • 2 New Characters
  • either 2 or 10 new weapons 🤷‍♂️
  • 3 New Darkanas
  • 1 New Music Track
  • 3 new Relics, of which 1 Secret rather than Unlockable

Other tweaks and features

  • "Random LevelUp" can now be toggled during a run if it is already unlocked on the Stage menu
  • Added option to Unbanish a weapon when picking it up from the stage
  • Buffed a few weapons like Magi-Stone and Mille Bolle Blu
  • Rendering fixes for a few weapons, including birds, Prismatic Missile, Runetracer…
Patch 1.15 will be released on all other platforms a bit later, by the end of the month, due to platform-specific optimizations and differences in save slots management. On the bright side, we will also be releasing a Nintendo Switch 2 version, with better performance and mouse support!

Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is coming Summer 2026

https://store.steampowered.com/app/4781330/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Bloodmoon/ Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is our “accidental” next expansion and the evil twin to Legacy of the Moonspell. The original plan was just to make a little content update to Legacy of the Moonspell. Since it’s the first and smallest VS expansion, it felt right to try to balance its value a little. Needless to say, ideas started to flow and everything spiraled into a much bigger project. I’m not sure I’ll ever learn at this stage. In the end, Legacy of the Moonspell will be getting its content buff (7 new unlocks) and Legacy of the Bloodmoon will live a life of its own. This expansion pack follows Clan Bloodmoon as they retrace the pilgrimage of Saint Baal’Thasar, in search of a paradise lit by (you guessed it) a bright red moon. There is also an ancient manor that may or may not hide the secret of immortality. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will contain:
  • 12 new villains friendly characters
  • 16+ new weapons and evolutions, including a FireBall
  • 8 savage new music tracks
  • 1 new adventure
  • 1 new very large stage
  • Interesting bits and bobs I won’t spoil at this time
But there’s more. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will cost approximately 1 money (0.99 USD), and Legacy of the Moonspell will receive a price cut and also be priced 1 money :) You can find all details about Legacy of the Bloodmoon below, now here’s a villainous trailer about it:

Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton

Among the many projects we’re working on (approximately 15 projects, not 15 games, please don’t panic) there is also a lineup of Survivaton games. It’s definitely a meaningful word that means “survive a ton” and nothing else. These are games like Vampire Survivors, developed internally at poncle, tied to IPs that might need unique game mechanics, a different graphic style, or are so expansive that ultimately deserve their own standalone game (compared to making a DLC for VS). I’d love to make examples, but I’d have to spoil way too much. Being developed internally, we’ll be able to guarantee affordability and worthwhile titles. Since a good 90% of global VS players aren’t reached by the Steam news (or are not interested in gaming news in general), the best way to also let them know that the Survivatons are tied directly to VS is to also call VS a Survivaton, hence the new sub-title. Please note there’s a dash before First Survivaton instead of a semi-colon, because DLCs exist... The next time I name a game I’ll remember to not use something as generic as “Monster Hunter” as inspiration please know I love Monster Hunter 💌

poncle Japan

We can finally say we are building poncle Japan! It will be poncle, but in Japan. The new studio is headed by Sawaki Takeyasu, known for his work on Devil May Cry, Ōkami, and El Shaddai: Ascension of the Metatron. Having a studio in Japan will simplify and speed up the work we do with all our Japanese partners, and also bring new opportunities for collabs. It’s too soon to say what the team will be working on; we are planning to fully open the studio by the end of 2026. Now it's time for all the FAQs and info blocks, thanks for reading and waiting patiently for this update! - Luca

Legacy of the Bloodmoon FAQs

When does it release? Summer 2026. What do you define as summer? Not winter. How much does it cost? Around £0.95, with regional pricing varying by platform and country. Why will Legacy of the Moonspell’s price change too? It felt right to adjust the price so that it’s more balanced compared to the amount of content of the other expansions. Please note that some stores have minimum prices in certain countries. In some places, Moonspell was already too cheap to make it cheaper. What about Tides of the Foscari then? Please at least wait for Moonspell and Bloodmoon before asking for more, we know we know 😭 Will Moonspell get new content too? Yes, 7 new unlocks for a few more weapons and characters. Is Vampire Survivors still getting free updates? Yes of course, there’s still plenty on the roadmap.

Update 1.15 Full spoilers

♫ Murder on the Seafloor Composed and arranged by Filippo Vicarelli.

Quick content guide:

  • Collect a total of 50 Vacuums to unlock The Lycaeum stage
  • Find the Penshin Fatcha in The Lycaeum and see all its evolutions to unlock it permanently
  • Survive 20 minutes in The Lycaeum to unlock Para Kooleo
  • Trigger a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo to unlock Darkana VIII - Edge of the Earth
  • Buy the Survarocchi at the top of The Lycaeum to unlock them for any character
  • Buy the Green Eyes Vizard at the top of The Lycaeum to be able to find Bat Dragons in other stages
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon (Currently available in Mad Forest and Il Molise) to unlock the Unearthly Bolt wea;on
  • Evolve the Unearthly Bolt with a maxed Tirajisú to unlock Big Troubler
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon with Big Troubler and Arcana 0 - Game Killer to unlock Darkana 0 - Stake to your Heart
  • Survive 15 minutes in Inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups to unlock Darkana XIX - Heir of Fate
  • Defeat 2 unique Bat Dragons to unlock a new set of Survarots to purchase from Big Troubler

Detailed info

New stage: The Lycaeum An underwater-themed stage where you press some buttons, beat some crabs, run to the center, kill more things, press more buttons, don’t die. The Drowner can only be defeated via raw damage or by reaching the top of the stage. Hidden treasures can be collected only using Mad Groove or Lavatrix Machina. Teleporters become active after reaching the top once. New character: Para Kooleo Starts with a Move Speed and Duration bonus. When his HP drops below a certain threshold it triggers a Vacuum. He also likes to evolve weapons. He has an abundance of skins. New character: Big Troubler Loves gold and gets trigger happy when he gets gold. The gold also loves him and will protect him at all costs. New weapon: Penshin Fatcha & Tonno Subito / Tonnado / Tonn’omoto / Tonn’oddeeo / Tonne / Unsurpassed / Miracle of Multiplication. Starting weapon for Para Kooleo. Select one of six tuna forms. Evolve it from one to another, stacking stats as you go. Evolve at least once to transform all the Vacuums pickup into "Lavatrix Machina". Then, if you choose to, evolve into the secret evolution, Miracle of Multiplication where everything happens at once. Does not require any items to evolve, but many, many treasure chests. New weapon: Unearthly Bolt & Spirit Disturbance Starting weapon of Big Troubler. Spawns green bolts that attack the closest enemy. It deals increasingly high damage if it Crits in rapid succession. The cap for this damage bonus is determined by Revivals. Evolve with a maxed out Tirajisú. The evolution spawns a green dragon that always deals critical hits. New relic: Green Eyes Vizard Bat Dragons will appear on the Stage Selection menu until they have been defeated at least once. They will appear on the map during a run, and they have to be activated by getting hit. Once active, time stops and enemy waves are changed until they are killed. You can fight them again in new runs, they simply won't be signaled in Stage Selection anymore after getting killed once. New Darkanas: 0 - Stake to your Heart Unlocked by defeating a Bat Dragon with Big Troubler while using the Game Killer Arcana. You will no longer be able to level up using experience gems. Instead, when defeating an enemy, they will also drop a Gold Coin, that you’ll be able to spend at a special merchant to buy weapons. Gold coins will also become your health: don't reach 0 (and quit before Red Death deals the usual 65535 damage per hit to you) New Darkanas: VIII - Edge of the Earth Unlocked by triggering a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo. Gain Thorns and Move Speed locked at 200%, ignore walls, destroy light sources upon contact, and attract things that normally aren’t attracted by a Magnet, like treasure chests. New Darkanas: XIX - Heir of Fate Unlocked by surviving 15 minutes in inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups enabled. While active, defeating enemies with Fire damage causes them to drop Scorched Souls. Additionally, a Nduja Fritta Tanto will trigger when the character's Health dips to a certain point. New Relics: Survarocchi Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum. Allows Survarot cards to spawn from light sources. Previously available only via the Ante Chamber dlc and a secret character, Survarots Enemahs (Secret rather than Unlockable) Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum after defeating any two unique Bat Dragons. Adds an extra 18 cards based on various enemies to drafts of Survarot. For the full list of bugfixes, please see here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1794680/view/693137145499484509

1.15 FAQs

How much is 1.15? It’s a free update. Can I now share DLCs when playing online? Not yet, in this patch we managed to do the groundwork to allow for DLC sharing, but we still have to complete the feature. Can I now use Cross-save on PS and Apple+? Not yet. We still don’t have the right policies in place to do that. What platforms is update 1.15 available on? Update 1.15 is launching on Steam first. Other platforms are planned to follow by the end of the month, including Xbox, PlayStation 4/5, Nintendo Switch, Android, iOS, and Epic Games Store. Is update 1.15 coming to Nintendo Switch 2? Yes! Update 1.15 will bring Vampire Survivors to Nintendo Switch 2 for the first time. It won’t arrive at the exact same time as the other platforms, but the current plan is for Nintendo Switch 2 support to follow around two weeks after update 1.15 (but don’t hold us to that). Where are the new achievements? We will sort out the new Steam achievements in the next patch (they will pop automatically). Hey are you still updating Vampire Crawlers? Yes of course, it’s taking longer than expected to release the first QOL improvements patch and a cute looking roadmap because we got stuck for days trying to exit the game.

Tickets are available now.

Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube In This Edition, Poncle’s Matteo Sapio on: - Vampire Survivors spin-offs and tie-ins - Opening studios in Japan and Italy - Working on over 15 projects

During last week’s London Game Festival, I spoke with Matteo Sapio, the chief strategy officer at Vampires Survivors developer Poncle.

We were speaking in front of a live audience, and it was one of the most revealing interviews I’ve done since launching The Game Business . During out chat, Sapio announced:

That Vampire Survivors has now surpassed 27 million players

It has over 15 projects in active development (and even more in earlier stages)

It is licensing out its engine to other brands and studios to build ‘Survivors’ games based on popular IP

It has paused its third-party publishing plans

“Vampire Survivors came from a solo developer,” Sapio explains. “It was Luca Galante, who made a game for him and his friends. Vampire Survivors exploded, and in two or three months, it sold more than one million copies. Luca’s yachts are video games. So instead of buying a yacht, he made the Emerald Beyond DLC [for Vampire Survivors] with Square Enix, which we released for free. Things grew organically from there.”

For more surprising developer interviews, sign-up to The Game Business today

First, there are spin-offs to Vampire Survivors. This includes the deck-building card battler Vampire Crawlers, which is out this week.

“We [are using] the famous Vampire Survivors IP to experiment in new genres,” Sapio tells us. “We love card games, but we are not very good at card games. They’re complicated. So, we made the game that we wanted to play.”

Vampire Crawlers is out this week Second, Poncle is working on original IP. Sapio says the company is currently developing two entirely original properties.

And third , there will be a range of new ‘Survivors’ games based on other IP. These are Vampire Survivors-like games set in other universes. Some will be developed by Poncle, whereas others – such as the upcoming Warhammer Survivors – are in collaboration with other studios.

Today, we are releasing Vampire Crawlers, a new spin-off set in the Vampire Survivors universe.

It takes the familiar chaos of Vampire Survivors and turns it into a casual, turn-based, card-driven BLOBBER with roguelite elements.

We’ve talked before about wanting to take some of the accidental core pillars of Vampire Survivors and apply them to other genres: accessibility, immediacy, affordability, replayability, lightheartedness, and the usual amount of flashy nonsense. Vampire Crawlers is the first attempt at that. 

Crawl through dungeons, build busted decks, master the TurboTurn™, and try to keep the run going long enough to pretend it was all planned. You can watch the launch trailer below.

(In other news, God appears briefly and remains unhelpful.)

Vampire Crawlers

The full game includes everything from the demo, plus more content, more fixes, and more improvements across the board. The game is built around:

  • TurboTurn™ combat: Turn-based combat without the wait. Queue your moves instantly and let the game resolve them at full speed.

    [/*]

  • The Combo: cards are played in ascending mana order, and each step multiplies the next card’s effect

    [/*]

  • Wild cards that let you extend the stack and push combos further

    [/*]

  • Deckbuilding through progression: level up to gain new cards, find power-ups, chase evolutions, and customize your runs

    [/*]

  • Character cards and summoned survivors that add more effects and help create larger cascades

    [/*]

  • Dungeon exploration with treasures, floor progression, and interactive points of interest

    [/*]

  • A pace you choose yourself: take your time and be tactical, or play turns as fast as you humanly can

    [/*]

The full version also launches with the fixes and improvements made after the demo feedback period, and we are planning to keep the demo available as well.

So all of us at poncle and Nosebleed Interactive would like to say thank you to everyone who played the demo, reported bugs, shared feedback, and generally tried to break things. That was genuinely useful.

Releasing now — $9.99 / €9.99 / £9.99

You can get Vampire Crawlers on Steam by clicking the link below.

Vampire Crawlers Original Soundtrack

Also releasing into the wild: the Vampire Crawlers Original Soundtrack.

The OST includes the game’s main theme, “Il Cuor non si Spaura,” composed by Yoko Shimomura, alongside tracks by Daniele Zandara, Filippo Vicarelli, and Michael Coviello. For a total of 32 tracks and over 1 hour of music for crawling purposes, available in MP3 and FLAC on Steam. It includes both the Crawling and Turbo versions, hidden tracks that are no longer hidden, and yes, there is a disco version of the inn theme.

  • What platforms is the game on? Vampire Crawlers is available on Steam, Nintendo Switch, Xbox, and PlayStation. Mobile versions are planned for later in 2026.

    [/*]

  • How long to beat the game? Around 20 to 30 hours, and a bit longer if you are going for every unlock.

    [/*]

  • Does the game support controllers? Yes. Controller support is included.

    [/*]

  • Does the game support cross-save between different platforms? Not right now, but we’re looking into it in time for the mobile ports.

    [/*]

  • Will save data carry over on Steam if I played the demo? Yes. Demo progress can carry over to the full game on Steam.
